sources.solution: Let larger a and smaller b: a+b=13, a-b=2, so a=7.5,b=5.5. Both sum and positive difference checked.
Length L,width W: 2(L+W)=30 and L-W=1 => L=8,W=7 metres. Half-perimeter is 15, not 30.
Oats O and buckwheat B: O+B=700,O-B=60 => O=380,B=320 hectares. Keep species and asked order.
A+B=187,A-B=23 => Model A=105, Model B-80=82 tractors. Both integer counts and exact total checked.
Wins w and draws d, no losses: w+d=11,2w+d=17 => w=6,d=5. The explicitly supplied historical points rule is authoritative, not a modern league rule.
Ski-pair price s and skate-pair price i: 3s+4i=47,2i-s=1 => s=9,i=5 dollars. Two skate pairs, not one, cost one dollar more than one ski pair.
Pen p and pencil-box c in dollars: 5p-2c=2.55,2p-5c=-1.50. Eliminate c:21p=15.75 => p=0.75,c=0.60. Check 3.75-1.20=2.55 and 1.50-3.00=-1.50.

Constant per-minute rates a,b in hectolitres:20a+10b=120,15a+7b=88.5. First 2a+b=12; substitute gives a=4.5,b=3. Check90+30=120 and67.5+21=88.5. No initial water is asserted in this rate word problem.
First x,second y: x+y/2=65 and y-x/3=x => y=4x/3. Thus5x/3=65 => x=39,y=52;52-13=39.

Original donor x and recipient y: x+y=16, after transfer x-6=(y+6)/3. Therefore3x-18=22-x => x=10,y=6; afterwards4 and12, ratio one-third. Source need not name the children; keep donor/recipient order.
1.20-dollar fruit mass a and1.50-dollar fruit b: a+b=36,1.2a+1.5b=1.3*36=46.8 => b=12,a=24 kilograms. Weighted mixture price, not arithmetic mean of unequal masses.
31-cent flour a and46-cent flour b: a+b=50,31a+46b=40*50=2000 cents => b=30,a=20 kilograms. Exact masses satisfy both total and value.
Autumn a and spring s hectares: a-s=480; unharvested 0.2a is300 less than0.75s, so0.75s-0.2a=300. Substitute a=s+480:0.55s=396 => s=720,a=1200. Remaining240 and540 differ300.
Planned outputs p for20%-over group and q for15%-over group: p+q=680,0.2p+0.15q=118 => p=320,q=360. Actual384 and414 total798; the source asks planned320/360, not actual outputs.
